Day 1
From Hotel: 10 min · 4 min → Praia do Camilo
1. Praia do Camilo
A pocket beach framed by golden cliffs and reached by a much-photographed wooden staircase of around 200 steps. The descent opens onto turquoise water and a rock tunnel through to a second cove — the most striking small beach within walking reach of town.
Open 24/7

2. Ponta da Piedade
Lagos's signature headland: ochre cliffs, sea stacks and arches dropping into clear water, with a 1913 lighthouse and a flat boardwalk along the rim. Railed platforms hang over the coves; a boat through the grottoes below is the classic way to see the formations up close.

3. Forte da Ponta da Bandeira
A compact 17th-century sea fort guarding the mouth of the harbour, reached by a short bridge over the water. Its ramparts open clean views back over the bay and the old town walls, and inside is a small exhibition on the Portuguese age of discovery.

3 min · 2 min → Igreja de Santo António
4. Igreja de Santo António
A small 18th-century church with an interior of breathtaking talha dourada — gilded carved woodwork over every surface, a painted barrel vault and blue-and-white azulejos. Entered through the municipal museum, it ranks among the finest baroque interiors in Portugal and is a national monument.

Day 2
From Hotel: 35 min → Fortaleza de Sagres
1. Fortaleza de Sagres
A windswept clifftop fortress on Henry the Navigator's promontory, where Portugal planned its 15th-century voyages of discovery. Inside the walls lie the giant pebble compass rose and a lone chapel, with the Atlantic crashing on three sides.
Read more
Daily 9:30am - 8:00pm
~1 hr 30 min
Promontório de Sagres · Sagres
8 min → Cabo de São Vicente
2. Cabo de São Vicente
The southwesternmost point of mainland Europe — sheer 75-metre cliffs the Romans called the Sacred Promontory, capped by a powerful lighthouse. Sunset here, where the land simply ends at the Atlantic, is among the most dramatic on the continent.
Read more
Daily 10:00am - 6:00pm
~1 hr

Day 3
From Hotel: 13 min → Passadiços de Alvor
1. Passadiços de Alvor
A wooden boardwalk threading through the salt marshes and tidal channels of the Ria de Alvor nature reserve, one of the Algarve's richest wetlands for wading birds — flamingos, storks and plovers move through the mudflats depending on the season. The loop runs between the old town and the river mouth with the Alvor hills as a backdrop.
Read more
Open 24/7
~1 hr
Passadiços de Alvor · Ria de Alvor
9 min · 3 min → Castelo de Alvor
2. Castelo de Alvor
A ruined medieval castle above Alvor's old town, raised by the Moors and rebuilt after the Christian conquest of 1189 — part of the same coastal defence line as the greater fortress at Silves. Little survives beyond a stretch of curtain wall and a watchtower, but the platform looks clean over the whitewashed rooftops to the Ria de Alvor beyond.
Read more
Open 24/7
~30 min
Largo do Castelo · Alvor
18 min · 5 min → Praia dos Três Irmãos
3. Praia dos Três Irmãos
The most dramatic beach in Alvor's parish — golden coves divided by sea arches and rock stacks carved from the same soft limestone as Ponta da Piedade, reached down a staircase cut into the cliff face. Caves and tunnels link several of the coves at low tide.
Read more
Open 24/7
~1 hr
80 steps · no lift
Praia dos Três Irmãos · Alvor
12 min → Meia Praia
4. Meia Praia
Lagos's own beach: four kilometres of open golden sand running east from the marina to the mouth of the Alvor estuary — the widest stretch of coastline in the western Algarve, backed by dunes rather than cliffs. The size keeps it uncrowded even in August, and kiosks along the promenade rent kayaks, paddleboards and windsurf gear.

Open 24/7
~1 hr 30 min

Day 4
From Hotel: 26 min → Carvoeiro
1. Carvoeiro
A former fishing village turned resort town wrapped around a small cove beach, with a cliffside boardwalk linking a run of coves and the sinkhole rock formations of Algar Seco just west of the harbour. Praia do Carvalho, reached through a tunnel cut into the rock, is the prettiest of the coves — and boats leave the beach for the Benagil cave system and Praia da Marinha's arches.

Praia do Carvalho · Carvoeiro
21 min · 8 min → Praia da Marinha
2. Praia da Marinha
Rated among the most beautiful beaches in Europe by National Geographic and the Michelin Guide — a small cove of pale sand walled in by two soaring limestone headlands riddled with arches, caves and sea stacks. A steep staircase down the cliff face is the only way in, and the view from the clifftop platform above is as celebrated as the beach itself.

14 min → Forte de São João do Arade
3. Forte de São João do Arade
A 16th-century fort guarding the mouth of the Arade river, its ochre walls rising straight out of the water opposite Portimão — one of the most photographed views on this stretch of coast. Privately owned and closed to visitors, it is seen from the quiet fishing village of Ferragudo, whose whitewashed lanes climb the hill behind it.

ARRIVE Silves: 27 min · 7 min → Castelo de Silves
1. Castelo de Silves
The red-sandstone citadel of the former Moorish capital of the Algarve — one of the best-preserved Arab fortifications in Portugal, its walls enclosing a hilltop of excavated cisterns and archaeological digs above a tangle of old streets. Silves fell to Christian forces in 1189 after a bloody siege, then again in 1249 for good.
Read more
Daily 9:00am - 8:00pm
~1 hr
Rua do Castelo · Silves
3 min · 1 min → Sé de Silves
2. Sé de Silves
Considered the main Gothic monument of the Algarve, built from 1268 on the site of the city's great mosque after the Christian reconquest. King John II lay buried at the high altar until his remains were moved to the Monastery of Batalha; the nave was only finished in the early 16th century.

Local Tastes
Cataplana
The Algarve's signature stew, slow-cooked and served in the hinged copper pan it is named for — clams, fish or seafood with peppers, and sometimes pork, steamed in their own juices.
A Forja · Adega da Marina
Dom Rodrigo
A glossy Algarve sweet of fine egg threads bound with almond, sugar and cinnamon, traditionally twisted into a brightly coloured foil wrapper.
Mercado Municipal
Medronho
A fiery clear spirit distilled from the berries of the strawberry tree, made in the hills of Monchique behind Lagos and poured as the local digestif.
Mercado Municipal
Food Delivery
Uber Eats
Foreign number: accepted. — the SMS code reaches international numbers; signing in with Google or Apple skips the code entirely.
Wide delivery coverage across the historic center and marina area. Restaurant selection includes seafood restaurants, casual beach joints and international options near the old town.
ubereats.com
Glovo
Foreign number: not required. — it signs in with Google, Facebook or email, and a phone sign-up takes any prefix with the code by SMS or WhatsApp.
Broad restaurant network in the Algarve including bakeries and local seafood places not always found on Uber Eats. Delivery zones cover the historic center and marina.
glovoapp.com
Bolt Food
Foreign number: accepted. — Bolt sends the sign-up code to international numbers; signing in with Google skips the verification step.
The ride app's delivery arm with reasonable coverage of Lagos. Smaller restaurant selection than Uber Eats or Glovo but useful as a backup when the others show longer wait times.
food.bolt.eu
Getting Around
Bolt
Foreign number: accepted. — Bolt sends the six-digit sign-up code to international numbers; signing in with Google skips the code entirely.
Reliable and affordable ride option throughout the Algarve. Well-established in Lagos with drivers covering the historic center, marina and outlying beach areas.
bolt.eu
Uber
Foreign number: accepted. — Uber's SMS code reaches foreign carriers; signing in with Google or Apple skips the verification step.
Available in the Algarve with decent driver supply during tourist season. Useful for reaching beaches outside walking distance and for evening returns from restaurants.

Day Trips by Train
Portimão · 20 min
A working riverfront city just up the line and the gateway to Praia da Rocha, where a boardwalk runs beneath honey-coloured cliffs and rock stacks. The old sardine-canning quay is now lined with grills.
book at: CP or Omio
Albufeira · 1h 5 min
The Algarve's most visited resort town, with a cliff-backed Old Town of whitewashed lanes above a beach, a lively marina, sea-cave boat trips and the famous Falesia beach to the east. The station at Ferreiras sits 6 km north of the centre; local buses and taxis connect in minutes.
book at: CP or Omio
Faro · 1 hr 40 min
The Algarve capital, with a walled old town of cobbled lanes, a cathedral you can climb, a macabre bone chapel, and boats out into the Ria Formosa lagoon and its islands.
book at: CP or Omio
Tavira · 2 hr 30 min
A graceful eastern-Algarve town of whitewashed churches straddling a river crossed by a Roman-era bridge, with a castle viewpoint and a ferry out to the sandbar beaches of Ilha de Tavira.
book at: CP or Omio
Vila Real de Santo António · 2 hr 45 min
The end of the line, a grid-planned 18th-century border town on the Guadiana river facing Spain across the water — a five-minute ferry crosses to Ayamonte. Manueline-style riverside gardens and a regular, walkable street plan make it unlike any other Algarve town.
book at: CP or Omio

Worth Knowing

The Edge of the Known World

The first two days of this trip trace a single thread without meaning to. The caravels that opened the Age of Discovery were rigged and crewed out of Lagos; the school of navigation that plotted their routes sat on the Sagres promontory of Day 2; and Cape St. Vincent was, for centuries, the literal edge of the known world — the last cliff before the blank part of the chart. Day 1 is the harbour the ships left from, Day 2 is the headland they aimed past.

It also rewards a little timing. The cliffs of Ponta da Piedade glow warmest in late-afternoon light, and Cape St. Vincent is the classic sunset cliff — so if Day 2's drive runs long, that is the cape working in your favour, not against it. Arrive at the lighthouse for the last hour of light and the wind, the cliffs and the falling sun do the rest.

Days 3 and 4 read the same coastline at two different scales. Alvor and Meia Praia on Day 3 are the version of the Algarve Lagos itself belongs to — wide sand, a tidal estuary, a modest ruin — all within ten minutes of the marina. Day 4 drives east into Lagoa municipality for the version tour buses queue up for: Praia da Marinha and the Carvoeiro coast are the postcard the whole region is sold on, and they earn it.

Day 5 is the one day this trip leaves the coast. Silves was the Moorish capital of the Algarve before Faro ever was — its red-sandstone castle is older and better preserved than anything built after the Reconquest, and the cathedral standing on its former mosque is the same layering of conquest and reconquest seen at Sagres, just built in stone instead of stood on a cliff. The direct train line means the whole day trip costs less than a tank of petrol and returns to the marina by nightfall.
